To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Mitochondrial morphology changes in Agrp and POMC neurons upon fasting, re-feeding, and overeating; (2) Mitochondrial dynamics are regulated by mitofusins in a cell-type specific manner in Agrp and Pomc neurons; (3) Mitochondrial fusion in Agrp neurons is essential for their activity and energy metabolism during overeating; and (4) Mitochondrial dynamic defects in Agrp neurons result in reduced fat mass and body weight

1) mitochondrial dynamics in Agrp neurons is cell-type specific, 2) mitofusins are required to maintain mitochondrial dynamics, and 3) mitofusin-mediated mitochondrial dynamics is important in the control of Agrp neuronal activity and diet-induced obesity.
mitochondrial fusion and fission proteins control the mitochondrial dynamics in Agrp neurons and that this control is important for the regulation of Agrp neuronal activity and energy homeostasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of energy metabolism in neurons.
the role of mitochondria in the regulation of energy homeostasis and obesity, which is a major public health problem worldwide.
the role of mitochondrial dynamics in energy homeostasis and obesity.

mitochondria in Agrp and POMC neurons undergo distinct fusion/fission dynamics in response to feeding conditions and that these changes in mitochondria morphology are important for the control of energy metabolism.
the size and the number of mitochondria are tightly controlled in Agrp neurons during the fasted to fed and the fed to overfed transition.
mitochondria in Agrp neurons are highly dynamic and that their fusion is required for proper neuronal activity and body weight control.
